messages.reasoning_content:
So we have:
- 527 customer contacts, 527 distinct customers, 105 with Contact priority = 1
- 630 complaints
- 428 tickets

Now, the complaints_table has "Work Order ID" which links to service_ticket_table. The complaints_table doesn't have a Customer ID directly. So to link complaints to customers, we need to go through the service_ticket_table (Work Order ID → Customer ID? No, service_ticket_table has Work Order ID, Contract ID, ...). Hmm, the service_ticket_table doesn't have a Customer ID either. It has Contract ID. So we need to join through contracts_table (Contract ID → Customer ID).

Wait, let me re-check the schema:
- complaints_table: Complaint Content ID, Work Order ID, Complaint Type Serial Number, Complaint Submission Time, Complaint Acceptance Time, Complaint Handler Employee ID, Complaint Handling Plan ID, Complaint Resolution Time, Complaint Customer Satisfaction, Whether Complaint Was Escalated, Complaint Handling Speed
- service_ticket_table: Work Order ID, Contract ID, Ticket handling agent ID, Ticket submission time, Ticket processing urgency level, Ticket priority, Ticket resolution time, Ticket resolution duration, Ticket customer satisfaction score, Whether the ticket had a second follow-up
- contracts_table: Contract ID, Customer ID, ...

So the linkage: complaints.Work Order ID = service_ticket.Work Order ID, service_ticket.Contract ID = contracts.Contract ID, contracts.Customer ID = customer_contact.Customer ID.

Alternatively, maybe sales_follow_up_table has Customer ID and Work Order ID. Yes! sales_follow_up_table: Follow-up Record Code, Customer ID, Work Order ID, ... So we can link Work Order ID → Customer ID through sales_follow_up_table as well.

Let me check which is more complete. Let me explore the data.

Let me check:
1. How many complaints can be linked to customer via sales_follow_up_table?
2. How many via service_ticket → contract → customer?
3. How do these compare?
